analysis:
The only changed file is docs/architecture/inference.md; there are no code, config or mode changes. The changes visible in the supplied units (head lines 632-638 and 882-918) describe three behaviors: (1) out-of-order prefill observation handling in EnginePerformanceMeasurements.Rate, keeping freshness anchored to the newest observation; (2) per-batch-step decode charging for deadline admission (CBv2DecodeRateShape); (3) a bound on the isolated prefill rate by the startup calibration idle rate, a 30-minute expiry for evidence on an idle engine, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 rollback. All of this is first-content deadline and admission estimation. It touches availability and performance routing only, and none of it touches the TB-002 encryption, T-041 prefix-cache, or T-053 App Attest authorization paths.

I found no security regression in the prose. The statements stay consistent with existing controls: physical KV admission and actual deadline expiry still apply, reviewed deadline profiles are unchanged, and the deadline catalog is empty. The DARKBLOOM_* rollback env var is covered by the existing DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification guard, which rejects unrecognized performance-affecting settings.

An adversarial provider can already skew self-reported performance (T-007 class). This documentation does not materially change that exposure, and nothing in it changes encryption, authorization or cache scoping.

Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and the actual code in AdmissionRateEstimators.swift and the engine was not supplied. Whether the described behavior matches the implementation is unverified. Any accompanying code change that makes admission less conservative should be reviewed for resource-exhaustion or deadline-gaming implications. This is documentation-only evidence.
